title: Establish pin & fallback checklist for onboarding experimental open models
creator: Priya Shah
description: Clarify and lock acceptance criteria and stepwise checklist for onboarding new open-source model variants into the Model Catalog. Focus areas: explicit version pin semantics, documented compatibility notes (tokenizer, KV cache, ABI), automated tests, and UI surface to expose pin/fallback choices to customers.
background: Multiple recent model submissions exposed ambiguity in how we represent 'compatible variants' and what it means to pin to a model version. Engineering requests a concise checklist and acceptance bar so Dedicated/Private customers can safely pin to a specific build while hosted customers benefit from fallback strategies. This ticket consolidates PM requirements to unblock engineering work in ENG-1842 and the onboarding flow updates in PM-11647.
requirements: Define canonical version identifier: {model_name}@{semver}+commit (e.g., llama2-7b@1.4.2+githash) and require an immutable artifact reference per catalog entry.
Document tokenization contract: tokenizer file(s), tokenizer config (normalization, add_prefix_space), tokenizer test vectors and a normalized tokenizer compatibility score (pass/fail).
Specify runtime compatibility flags: required kv_cache_schema, attention format, supported backend kernels, and maximum supported sequence length.
Pinning semantics: UI and API must allow 'strict pin' (exact semver+commit) and 'pinned major' (major.minor wildcard only when SDK/ABI guarantees equivalence).

Fallback rules: define explicit ordered fallback chain: strict pin -> compatible variant -> nearest minor with conversion -> fallback model (smaller/cheaper). Each fallback step must record reason and applied transformation in request metadata.

Automated validation: each onboarding must include a CI job that runs canonical prompt set (10 prompts), checks tokenization diffs, output-size regression (<5% tokens), and latency baseline vs catalog entry (within 1.5x).
Migration guidance: provide a one-page doc for customers describing migration steps when a pinned variant is superseded (including sample API calls to update pin), and recommended rollback steps.
Console surface: add a model detail card showing the recommended_pin, compatibility summary, and an 'Apply strict pin' toggle with warning modal.
acceptance_criteria:
1) PRD and onboarding checklist published in Confluence and linked from the catalog onboarding UI.
2) GitHub onboarding template updated to require tokenizer test vectors and artifacts_uri (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/model-catalog/pull/1234).
3) ENG CI job implemented and green for representative new-model PR (run id referenced in links).
4) UX mock for pin/fallback toggle reviewed and signed off by Design (see Figma link).
5) Console shows compatibility notes for at least two newly onboarded open models and allows strict pinning in staging.
6) Acceptance tests: tokenization diffs < 1% for allowed variants, latency within 1.5x baseline, and automated regression tests added to runtime-1.20 pipeline.
scope_changes: Start scope restricted to open-source model variants only (no closed/third-party licensed models) for initial rollout. Excludes automated quantization conversion—this will be handled in a follow-up (PM-12045).
tradeoffs: We tighten pinning semantics (favoring safety) which increases friction for model maintainers; to mitigate, provide a small helper script to generate required artifacts and test vectors. Strict pin enforcement may reduce automatic availability of new performance improvements unless operators explicitly update pins.
decisions: 2026-03-11: Agreed on canonical version identifier format (semver + commit hash). — Priya

2026-03-12: Console will expose both 'strict pin' and 'pinned major' options; default for hosted catalog entries will remain 'managed' unless user explicitly pins. — Design + PM
